detail:
The standalone compaction output is itself a clean measurement, because post-1.24.0 files carry exactly 1 junk entry each (the loop is fixed) so "kept" counts are genuine content. Recent field sweeps: 2026-07-16 442 kept, 07-26 500, 07-29 500, 07-31 500. That is 500 archivable entries swept every 2-3 days, i.e. ~250/day. The trigger (blackboard.ts:163-180, threshold config.ts:49 = 500) counts only archivable entries — decisions, archive-tagged entries, and UNRESOLVED needs/warnings are excluded — so these 500-entry sweeps are real findings, statuses, questions, answers, and resolved obligations. CONSEQUENCE: findings in this project have a ~2-3 day half-life before leaving every live retrieval surface. This is the uncontaminated evidence for the archive concern that the 9.1M junk number obscured, and it RAISES the priority of the retention fix. It also sharpens the design: at ~250 archivable/day, no fixed threshold gives a long window (a 14-day age cutoff would mean ~3,500 live entries, which assemble reads in full on every call). Trimming to newest-K only doubles the horizon. The durable fix is making the archive a QUERYABLE COLD TIER (separate embedding index, assemble opts in when live results are thin) rather than tuning the threshold. Compaction result: 9,136,128 junk dropped, 3.57 GB reclaimed, 6,501 real entries preserved, 4 all-junk files removed, live board untouched.</detail>
